S1.requirement: Brian additive Euler, stochastic Heun and Milstein with original restrictions
S1.source_reasoning: The frontend calls the registered Brian built-in integrator, preserving its stochastic restrictions. The reference injects the addressed native draws into Brian; the independent oracle spells out Euler, Heun and Milstein updates.

S2.requirement: Multistate/shared/named noise and state/parameter diffusion VJPs with time/refractory/full/TBPTT
S2.source_reasoning: Named streams are bound to state programs; state and parameter dependence remains in the differentiable expression graph. The fixed-noise oracle perturbs every parameter bank and initial state, with separate full and truncated reverse paths.

S3.requirement: Native independent RNG addresses, replay, sequence/carry, partition invariance and failure/readonly atomicity
S3.source_reasoning: Random addresses include seed, sequence, sample, domain, entity, tick and stream, never rank or draw order. Forward and reverse reuse these addresses. Only successful train commits persistent state; fresh readonly operations now preserve lazy initialization and checkpoint bytes.

S4.requirement: Checkpoint/fresh-process restore, CPU/Metal/CUDA/localMPI and independent forward/FD/backend evidence
S4.source_reasoning: Checkpoints include optimizer, physical state, clocks, noise and Poisson caches and bind the native runtime. Restore checks identities before commit. The stochastic replay test also restores in a new Python process and compares split continuation.

D1.requirement: Per-edge continuous/event states separate from optimizer parameters; neuronal state reads
D1.source_reasoning: Mutable per-edge variables receive physical runtime cells; trainable initial values have separate optimizer bindings. Built-in continuous integration and exact event updates are lowered into actions that also read endpoint state.

D2.requirement: pre/post order, dynamic transmission, STDP and STP with correct initial/parameter separation
D2.source_reasoning: Actions follow Network.sorted_objects. Each ordinary pathway composes exact event advance, ordered user assignments and final lastupdate. The STP reference uses the newly updated u for release before resource depletion.

D3.requirement: Whole-path gate VJP, all-state across-time gradients, surrogate/clip/detach/TBPTT rules
D3.source_reasoning: The tape holds each pre-action context; reverse traverses visits and actions in reverse order. Gate derivatives use the entire composed output minus its old value; clip/min/max use explicit piecewise rules and declared detach/TBPTT boundaries clear adjoints.

D4.requirement: carry/store/restore, masks/freeze, MPI ownership/reduction and actual GPU execution
D4.source_reasoning: Explicit carried state bypasses optimizer initial bindings. Mask migration and checkpoints preserve physical state. Owner GPU phases compute and collectively apply each action, then reduce parameter gradients before the train-only optimizer commit.

D5.requirement: Nonzero delay queues, summed states and random synapse combinations without silent static substitution
D5.source_reasoning: Delay histories are physical state and route arrival gates into the same action graph; old arrivals survive route migration. Summed actions clear then accumulate at their original schedule position. Noise is addressed by edge/domain and reused by reverse.

C1.requirement: Runtime edge states are distinct from optimizer parameters; carry cannot reinstall learned initialw
C1.source_reasoning: Optimizer initial bindings are installed only when an explicit runtime initial state is absent. A carried w therefore keeps its plasticity value instead of being overwritten by a learned initial parameter.

C2.requirement: Full ordered action maps with edge state/context tape; preserve pre/post schedule
C2.source_reasoning: Sequential statements substitute updated local expressions into later statements and produce simultaneous final outputs. Each action tapes its source context before writeback; reverse uses this tape rather than later mutable state.

C3.requirement: Event-driven exact advance witht-lastupdate before path; discrete lastupdate, differentiable decay parameters
C3.source_reasoning: Brian linear supplies event-driven exact evolution with dt replaced by t-lastupdate. That evolution precedes the user path; lastupdate=t follows it. Timestamp storage is detached, while tau remains a parameter leaf in the decay expression.

C4.requirement: summed clear/accumulate at actualgroups/order; preserve sorted continuous neuron/synapse schedule
C4.source_reasoning: Lowering iterates Brian sorted objects and emits summed target clearing immediately before original-edge accumulation. Continuous neuron/synapse actions retain their position and clock, rather than being moved to a common post-update phase.

C5.requirement: Independent dynamic IR/action sequence/full state layout/context reverse VJP and explicitclip rules shared across CPU/GPU
C5.source_reasoning: The dynamic schema has physical state, actions, program sets and context bindings. CPU executes these programs directly; GPU encodes the same nodes and programs. Reverse and clip rules are explicit, with capability checks rejecting incompatible device libraries.

C6.requirement: Hard forward events, surrogate/counterfactual reverse and detached timestamp gates
C6.source_reasoning: Thresholds produce binary hard forward spikes. Reverse applies the declared surrogate; ordinary event gates add a counterfactual whole-transform difference. Discrete time, refractory and explicitly detached triggers have no continuous gate derivative.

C7.requirement: Cross-partition state/adjoints preserve action order; actual owner/reduction and GPU, no silent CPU fallback
C7.source_reasoning: GPU MPI owner selection precedes action computation; other ranks contribute zero. The collective result is applied in action order to replicated state/adjoints. Missing GPU library or ABI is an error; execution never enters the CPU dynamic path as a fallback.

C8.requirement: Delayed queues/history across blocks and reverse to origin trigger tick; independent native neuron/edge/group RNG domains
C8.source_reasoning: Arrival gates read shifted history cells, whose reverse assignment chain reaches the emission state across visits. Carry retains the histories; migration retains pending generations. Event random addresses use emission tick or persistent imported-entry identity, separated from ordinary neuron streams.

E1.requirement: Each sequential edge/pathF(state) uses one event gate, not a separately smoothed gate per statement
E1.source_reasoning: The compiler composes one path into F before binding its trigger. CPU and GPU both compute the gate contribution as the sum of output adjoints times F(state)-state, so the gate is not applied independently to each source statement.

E2.requirement: Refractory masks neuron writes inside ordered path; plastic edge updates continue
E2.source_reasoning: Conditional-write flags become guards on individual target assignments inside composition. Later statements see the held or updated value. Unguarded edge-state updates remain in the same event path even when neuron writes are refractory-clamped.

E3.requirement: Autapse/pre/post/shared aliases retain local snapshots, final write order and merged VJPs
E3.source_reasoning: Brian logical alias names receive distinct pre-path locals even when they share physical cells. Sorted writeback retains the final physical winner. Reverse clears each physical destination once and accumulates all read-local adjoints into canonical storage.

E4.requirement: External evolving state has explicit input contract; no silent initial-constant substitution
E4.source_reasoning: External evolving fields require explicit TimedArrays with checked units, physical ownership and shape. Their reads become clock-sampled table-bank expressions with table VJPs; selected graph writes to imported storage are rejected, without replacing evolving fields by initial constants.
